data.title: Calculating Geodesic Pavilion Support Struts
data.subject: Algebra

problem.statement: An architectural firm is designing a modern geodesic pavilion where the total budget for structural reinforcement is allocated across a base infrastructure fee and customized support struts. The firm incurs a fixed overhead cost of \$4,500 for site preparation, and each manufactured strut incurs an additional variable fabrication cost of \$125. If the total project expenditure reaches \$11,875, determine the exact quantity of support struts manufactured by setting up and solving a linear equation.

inset.scenario: Determining the number of customized support struts manufactured based on fixed overhead site preparation and variable fabrication costs that equal the total project expenditure.

quantities.meaning: fixed overhead cost for site preparation in dollars
variable fabrication cost per strut in dollars

target.meaning: exact quantity of support struts manufactured

distractorEquations.misconception: Swapped operands by incorrectly applying the variable cost rate to the fixed overhead and treating the unit cost as a standalone constant.
Applied a sign flip by subtracting the fixed overhead cost instead of adding it to the total variable expenses.
Dropped the coefficient representing the variable cost per strut, treating each strut as contributing only one unit of value.

inset.rationale: The total expenditure is equal to the sum of the fixed site preparation overhead and the product of the variable cost per strut and the total number of struts manufactured.
inset.label: Equation Setup

data.solutionStrategy: Isolate the variable term by applying inverse operations in reverse order of operations to determine the exact quantity.

steps.title: Set up the linear equation
steps.strategy: Translate the real-world architectural costs and constraints into a mathematical model.
steps.misconceptions: Confusing the fixed overhead cost with the variable fabrication cost per strut.

steps.title: Isolate the variable term
steps.strategy: Use the inverse operation of addition to remove the fixed site preparation fee from the left side.
steps.misconceptions: Forgetting to subtract the fixed cost from the total expenditure on the right side.

steps.title: Solve for the number of struts
steps.strategy: Use the inverse operation of multiplication to isolate the variable representing the number of support struts.
steps.misconceptions: Dividing the total expenditure instead of the remaining cost after subtracting the overhead.

data.gradeLevel: middle school students (grades 6-8) - Use more complex vocabulary, abstract concepts, real-world applications, and critical thinking opportunities. Encourage deeper analysis.
